$A=\left[-\cos x-2\sin x\right]_\alpha^{\pi+\alpha}$
$=-\{\cos(\pi+\alpha)-\cos\alpha\}-2[\sin(\pi+\alpha)-\sin\alpha]$
$=2\cos\alpha+4\sin\alpha=2\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)+4\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)=\frac{10}{\sqrt{5}}$
Area enclosed by the two curves is $2\sqrt{5}$ sq. units
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Writes and evaluates, in simplest exact form, a definite integral for the area between the curves; 2: Substantial progress eg. obtains the anti-derivative and evaluates in terms of alpha, beta; 1: Some progress eg. writes the definite integral and anti-derivative is partially correct

$a=2e^{-t}$, $v=-2e^{-t}+c$; $t=0,\ v=-1\Rightarrow -1=-2+c$ $\therefore c=1$ $\therefore v=1-2e^{-t}$
$x=t+2e^{-t}+d$; $t=0,\ x=2\Rightarrow 2=2+d$ $\therefore d=0$ $\therefore x=t+2e^{-t}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Uses integration to find required expressions for both v and x in terms of t; 1: Substantial progress eg. finds v in terms of t

solutions.latex: $v=0$, $e^{-t}=\frac{1}{2}$, $e^t=2$, $t=\ln 2$. $x=t+2e^{-t}=\ln 2+2\times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1+\ln 2$. At rest $(1+\ln 2)$ m to right of $O$ at time $\ln 2$ seconds.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Finds time and position when particle at rest; 1: Substantial progress eg. finds time when particle at rest

solutions.latex: $t=\ln 8\Rightarrow x=\ln 8+2e^{\ln\frac{1}{8}}=3\ln 2+\frac{1}{4}$. Hence in the first $\ln 8$ seconds, particle travels left $2-(1+\ln 2)$ metres, then is instantaneously at rest before moving off to the right (since $a>0$) travelling a further $\left(3\ln 2+\frac{1}{4}\right)-(1+\ln 2)$ metres. Required distance is $\left(\frac{1}{4}+\ln 2\right)$ metres.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Adds distances travelled left and right in the first ln8 seconds; 1: Substantial progress eg. finds simplified expression for x when t = ln8

solutions.latex: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\ln x}{x}\right)=\dfrac{\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\cdot x-(\ln x)\cdot 1}{x^2}=\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x^2}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: Applies an appropriate rule for differentiation

solutions.latex:
If $f(x)=\dfrac{\ln x}{x}$, then $\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}=\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x^2}\times\dfrac{x}{\ln x}=\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x\ln x}$
$\therefore\displaystyle\int_e^{e^2}\frac{1-x}{x\ln x}\,dx=\left[\ln\left(\frac{\ln x}{x}\right)\right]_e^{e^2}$
$=\left[\ln(\ln x)-\ln x\right]_e^{e^2}=\ln 2-\ln 1-(2-1)=\ln 2-1$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Recognises integration pattern to obtain anti-derivative as a log function then evaluates; 2: Substantial progress eg. obtains anti-derivative and partially evaluates; 1: Some progress eg. obtains anti-derivative
